skill.name: specs-creator
skill.description: Create structured PRDs, technical specs, and UX specs from feature requirements using bundled templates and validation guidance.
skill.summary: Create consistent product, technical, and UX specification documents from feature descriptions.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown formatting, placeholder template examples, and validation code. One medium-risk finding remains because the skill instructs agents to run bundled community validation scripts, which creates external command execution risk despite the scripts appearing purpose-built for local spec checks.

remediation.issue: Bundled validation scripts are executed as part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running validation scripts, and document the exact commands and file scope before execution.

remediation.issue: Template examples include placeholder secret and database environment variable names.
remediation.suggestion: Keep these values clearly marked as examples and instruct users never to place real secrets in generated specs.

content.user_title: Create Structured Product and Technical Specs
content.value_statement: Teams often lose feature details when requirements move from idea to implementation. This skill turns feature descriptions into structured PRDs, technical specs, and UX specs with validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates PRD, technical specification, and UX specification documents from feature requirements.
Uses separate templates for product, technical, and UX documentation.
Checks dependency order before creating later-stage specs.
Guides placement of generated specs in a designated specs directory.
Runs bundled validation scripts to check structure and dependencies when appropriate.
limitations: Does not implement application code or modify production features.
Requires clear feature requirements or follow-up clarification from the user.
Depends on local validation scripts and templates included with the skill.
Generated specs still need review by product, engineering, and design stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Draft a PRD for a new feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature idea into a structured product requirements document with goals, users, requirements, and success criteria.

use_cases.title: Prepare technical planning documents
use_cases.description: Convert approved product requirements into implementation-focused technical specs with architecture, APIs, data, testing, and deployment sections.

use_cases.title: Document UX expectations before build
use_cases.description: Create UX specifications that capture flows, visual systems, interaction states, accessibility needs, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for this feature: [describe the feature, target users, and main problem it solves]. Ask me for missing requirements before writing the final spec.

prompt_templates.title: Create a technical spec from a PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after product requirements exist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a technical specification for the approved PRD in specs/[prd file]. Include architecture, data model, API, security, testing, deployment, and rollback sections.

prompt_templates.title: Create UX specs for a feature flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create UX specifications for [feature name]. Cover user flows, design principles, component states, accessibility, responsive behavior, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a full spec chain
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for product, engineering, and design alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the complete spec set for [feature]. Start with dependency checks, then produce the PRD, technical spec, and UX spec in the required order. Validate each document and summarize gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a PRD for saved search alerts in our marketplace.
output_examples.output: A product requirements document with problem statement, goals, personas, user stories, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, success metrics, dependencies, and out-of-scope items.

output_examples.input: Create UX specs for onboarding after the PRD is approved.
output: A UX specification organized by design principles and user flows.
Component and interaction requirements for key screens.
Accessibility, responsive design, and state guidance for implementation review.

output_examples.input: Validate whether this technical spec is ready for engineering review.
output_examples.output: A review summary that identifies missing sections, unresolved placeholders, dependency issues, and recommended next steps before review.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, target users, constraints, and known dependencies before asking for a spec.
Create specs in dependency order so product decisions inform technical and UX details.
Review generated specs with stakeholders before treating them as implementation guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to write implementation code instead of documentation.
Do not skip clarification when requirements are incomplete or contradictory.
Do not overwrite existing specs unless the user explicitly approves the replacement.

faq.question: What kinds of specs can this skill create?
faq.answer: It can create product requirements documents, technical specifications, and UX specifications using included templates.

faq.question: Does it write application code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is scoped to documentation and validation guidance, not implementation changes.

faq.question: Can it work from a short feature idea?
faq.answer: Yes, but it should ask clarifying questions when important requirements are missing.

faq.question: Why does it mention dependency order?
faq.answer: The workflow expects product requirements before technical and UX specs, so later documents are based on approved context.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Are the generated specs final project decisions?
faq.answer: No. They are structured drafts that should be reviewed by product, engineering, and design stakeholders.
